text:
neha: Heads-up — EU2 p99 token latency spiked after last midnight deploy. Queue depth jumped ~3x, admit rate fell. Seeing egress retransmits to eu-cache. Trying to surface quick numbers.

sam: grafana? pls paste panel link

neha: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/EU2/ingress-latency (snippet)
```
summary: pre = 03:00-04:00 UTC, post = 04:00-05:00 UTC
p95: 220ms -> 1.1s
p99: 480ms -> 4.2s
queue depth: 120 -> 380
admit rate: 60 rps -> 18 rps
gpu-hours/day burn: +25% (estimate)
```

leo: NVLink / GPU mem saturation look OK? or is this pure network amplification + retries?

neha: NVLink/GPU util steady ~65%. egress queue to eu-cache shows socket drops + fast retries. app retry config was accidentally set to aggressive backoff (0.5s) after the proxy change.
```
retry_policy:
  attempts: 3
  initial_backoff_s: 0.5  # should be 2.0
  multiplier: 1.5
```

maria: If retries are amplifying, admit control must compensate. Proposal: tighten admit curve in EU2 (-20% threshold) + roll back retry initial_backoff to 2s. Quick cost/benefit?

sam: What's customer impact if we tighten admit by 20% (more drops)? p99 SLO is 99.9% for many routes. Need rough numbers.

neha: Quick calc: baseline arrival λ = 50 rps. Measured retry amplification factor R ≈ 0.6 (each failure triggers ~0.6 extra attempts) => effective λ' = λ*(1+R) = 80 rps. Our provisioned steady capacity c ≈ 60 rps. With λ' > c queue grows: (80-60)/60 ≈ 33% extra queueing per unit time. If we reduce retries to R=0.1 (via backoff), λ' -> 55 rps < c and queue drains.

maria: Numbers: tightening admit by 20% reduces effective c to 48 rps so short term we trade latency for dropped requests but avoid system meltdown. Expected GPU-hours saved vs leaving as-is ~30 GPU-hours/day (rough).

leo: Additional mitigation: route non-sensitive traffic to eu1 for 6h to take ~20% load off EU2. Egress cost tradeoff: extra inter-region egress ~ $0.12/hr per GPU but keeps p99 contained.

sam: Plan: 1) schedule canary to change retry initial_backoff 0.5->2.0 and enable soft-admit at 0.8 for EU2 (10% traffic). 2) monitor p95/p99 + queue depth 15/30m checkpoints. If stable, bump to 50% then full.

neha: Ops playbook: if p99 > 2s after 30m, abort and roll back; if p99 > 3s open incident. I'll watch logs and aggregate retry traces. tagging @oncall. :eyes:

ops-bot: action: canary scheduled by sam at 2026-03-20T02:30:00Z — canary id CAN-5923 — initial traffic 10% for 15m.

deploy-bot: about to create job: proxy-config-rollout/eu2/retry-backoff v1.2 -> v1.3 (canary)

sam: quick forecast note: if retry R drops from 0.6 -> 0.1 we expect effective arrival down from 80->55 rps. That reduces queueing and should save ~40 GPU-hours/day based on current traffic mix. I'll attach a more formal calc in PR.

maria: agree with this staged approach. Also schedule a traffic-shift runbook to route stateless workloads to eu1 if canary doesn't stabilize within 45m.

neha: I'll collect top 10 caller stacks and prefix cache keys causing retries. If we find a hot client, we can contact them directly. For now we're on canary watch. :thumbsup:
